title: Annotatio IV §.X open: Sixth century — end of better ages; Christian truth begins to decline
pass_a_gloss: §. X. We have reached the end of the better Ages, and the beginning of the worse — the SIXTH, I mean — in which the Christian matter and Truth began to rush into the worse; Wherefore it is not beside the point that Gerhard. Theodorus Mejerus, exhibiting his sixth Section, the History of the Christian Religion of the sixth Age, p. 164, begins thus §. I.
pass_b_english: §.X: we have reached the end of the better ages and the start of the worse — the SIXTH — when Christian truth began to rush downhill.
Mejerus opens his sixth section (Christian Religion of the sixth age, p. 164) with that framing.
source_text: §. X. Meliorum Seculorum finem attigimus, deterioremque initium, SEXTUM puta, quô res Veritasque Christiana in pejus ruere cœpit; Quare non præter rem Gerhard. Theodorus Mejerus, Sectionem suam sextam, Christianæ Religionis Seculi sexti Historiam exhibentem, p. 164. ita inchoat §. I.

lemmas.gloss: began to rush into the worse
